about.title: What is Satlas?
about.intro: Curious what satellites are passing over your country right now? This site answers that at a glance.

why.title: Why it exists
why.body: Most satellite trackers focus on what an observer can see from their own location. Few show what is flying over an entire country, so Satlas was built to fill that gap.

how.title: How it works
how.body: Each satellite's current position is computed from public orbital data (TLEs) using a standard propagation formula (SGP4). The resulting coordinate is then checked against country polygons to determine which country it falls over.
how.refresh: Catalog and orbit data are automatically pulled twice a day, and calculations restart from those fresh measurements. Satellites drift slightly over time due to atmospheric drag and small gravitational variations, so the longer the same computation runs forward, the more its result diverges from reality. Thanks to this refresh cycle, the residual position error stays very small within this site's 24-hour window.

limits.title: Limits
limits.body: Satellite categories follow the data source (CelesTrak) as-is. Classified satellites — for example reconnaissance — whose orbits are not public are not included. Country borders come from a public map dataset (Natural Earth) at a coarse resolution, so very small islands may be missing.

source.title: Sources
source.intro: Code and data are all open.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.body: Visitor statistics are handled by Vercel Analytics: cookieless, aggregate page views only. No personally identifiable information is collected.
